key_insight: Chest X-ray search works better when models learn the full clinical meaning of a query, including conjunctions and negations, not just keyword overlap.
clinical_relevance: This could make radiology image retrieval more accurate for clinicians searching large archives using short, real-world findings-based queries.
method: Built CXR-Retrieve, a benchmark for compositional chest X-ray text-to-image retrieval.
Defined relevance by whether an image satisfies all pathology constraints in the query, including positive and negative assertions.
Fine-tuned a label-aware contrastive model to pull together clinically compatible image-text pairs and push apart contradictory ones.
evidence_signal: The benchmark includes 5,159 MIMIC-CXR-JPG test images and 145 queries, and the proposed method improved Precision@5 by 8.5 points on two-finding conjunctions and 22.0 points on negation queries.
watch_item: Performance is reported on a specific benchmark and in-domain checkpoint, so real-world generalization to other institutions, report styles, or rare findings still needs validation.
paper_title: CXR-Retrieve: Compositional Text-to-Image Retrieval in Chest Radiography
